name: Episode 1 ruthless creator-parity gate
philosophy: technical correctness is necessary but never sufficient
every dimension is compared against observed competitor mechanics, not generic best practices
no aggregate score can hide a catastrophic weakness
human first-watch can veto any automated pass
success is not guaranteed; the gate only removes known flop risks and raises creative quality

dimensions.check: immediate visual conflict, surprise, motion, or curiosity before explanation
clear premise, stakes, entertainment promise, and momentum
meaningful visual evolution at competitive cadence; no decorative motion-only cheating
world/characters/objects move causally; no slideshow grammar
Alex reacts, initiates, fails, recovers, and physically interacts with concepts
finance concepts visibly cause consequences instead of being narrated over icons
each beat raises tension, absurdity, stakes, or consequence
frequent genuine resets: reveal, reversal, new problem, visual gag, question, payoff
jokes/punchlines/callbacks arrive often enough for entertainment-first identity
some jokes only work visually; narration is not doing all comedy
human rhythm, phrase-length variety, pauses used intentionally, no monotonous lecture tone
SFX/music/silence punctuate contact, reveals, reversals, tension, and jokes
cuts, pans, zooms, reframes, and transitions are motivated and varied
text amplifies impact or clarity and never becomes presentation slides
screen text is instantly readable and not duplicating narration in paragraphs
new chapters change action/location/problem/energy rather than title-card resets
recurring objects/jokes create memory and cohesion
ending rewards full watch with callback, escalation payoff, or memorable final joke
teaser creates curiosity without weakening current payoff
borrows mechanics only; does not clone protected characters, jokes, dialogue, sequences, or brand assets
financial mechanism is understandable without lecture pacing
claims and caveats remain accurate and not misleading
average viewer can follow without prior finance knowledge
surprise, tension, relief, embarrassment, victory, fear, absurdity rotate
contains memorable visual moments worth quoting, clipping, or sharing
no unintentional low-energy stretches or passive explanatory holds
no generic card grids, template transitions, over-clean iconography, repetitive poses, synthetic filler phrasing

automatic_rejects: any slideshow or card-deck sequence is the dominant grammar
three or more consecutive explanatory beats where narration advances but character/world does not
opening begins with context-setting before entertainment
static text or diagram holds longer than benchmark tolerance without intentional joke/tension
music/SFX function as wallpaper instead of timed storytelling
visuals repeat narration rather than add meaning
chapter changes are only headings or color swaps
character poses repeat enough to feel templated
disclaimers repeatedly interrupt momentum instead of being visually integrated
success_amplifiers: curiosity gap closed with satisfying payoff
physical metaphors for abstract finance mechanics
visual jokes that reward watching with sound off
location and energy changes between chapters
sound effects locked to visible contact
music energy changes at story turns
numbers transform physically rather than sit in tables
stakes become personal to Alex, not only mathematical
next-episode teaser after, not instead of, payoff
